Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Summary: We walked through the Redwood Hosted inference flow for your customer support assistant use case (short answers, entity extraction, and reranking).
- Key constraints you called out: 1) sub-300ms p95 token latency on user-facing responses, 2) strict PII handling and audit logs, 3) budget target ~ $0.002 per 1k tokens processed initially.

Attached are the benchmarks and the prompt sets we used during the demo. Below is a recommended shortlist with high-level rationale — we can iterate once you review with engineering.

Recommended shortlist (preliminary):
1) Redwood-Redwood-2.9B-quant (hosted) — Best balance of quality and cost for short-form answers. Estimated latency: ~180–250ms p95 (us-west), cost: moderate. Good first-choice for production pilots.
2) OpenLlama-13B-8bit (hosted variant) — Higher quality on complex queries, higher cost and latency (~350–450ms p95), useful for escalation flows.
3) Redwood-1.3B-FP16 (hosted) — Lowest cost and fastest latency (~100–150ms p95) for simple NLU and extraction tasks; watch for edge-case hallucinations.

Attachments: acme-demo-benchmarks-20270406.pdf, acme-prompt-sets-20270406.csv

- Can you confirm which flows you want in the initial pilot (agent replies only, or replies + reranking + extraction)?
- Are there security/POC requirements we should route to our Private deployment team (Dev cc'd)?
- I can schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk the benchmark numbers with Rishi and the infra folks.

Hi Alex — copying quick tech/ops answers inline and a concise comparison. Happy to walk this through live.

1) Redwood-2.9B-quant (hosted):
   - Cost: ~ $0.0018 per 1k tokens (token accounting includes input+output).
   - Latency (eu-west, steady-state, 1–4 token responses typical): p95 ~ 210–280ms with our pooled hosting; p50 ~ 90–120ms.
   - Notes: Quantized kernel gives good CPU/GPU throughput; we recommend enabling prefix caching if you expect repeated prompts.

2) OpenLlama-13B-8bit (hosted variant):
   - Cost: ~ $0.0045 per 1k tokens.
   - Latency (eu-west): p95 ~ 380–470ms.
   - Notes: Higher quality for complex reasoning and multi-turn context. Hosted variant supports KV caching; you can enable auto-batching but memory footprint is larger.

3) Redwood-1.3B-FP16 (hosted):
   - Cost: ~ $0.0009 per 1k tokens.
   - Latency (eu-west): p95 ~ 110–160ms.
   - Notes: Best for deterministic extraction and high throughput; expect lower raw language quality. Watch for hallucination on ambiguous prompts.

Security / PII:
- Ingestion-side redaction: We support configurable redact-at-ingest rules on both Hosted and Private. For Hosted, redaction happens before persistent logs are written if enabled; however, for strict compliance (no transit logs), Private deployment with customer-managed KMS is recommended. Dev — can you confirm the Private deployment checklist link?

Comparison summary (quality / latency / cost tradeoffs):
- Redwood-2.9B-quant: Balanced quality, mid-latency, mid-cost — recommended first pilot for reply accuracy and economics.
- OpenLlama-13B-8bit: High quality, higher latency/cost — use for escalation or internal-only higher-accuracy flows.
- Redwood-1.3B-FP16: Low cost, low latency, lower quality — good for extraction and bulk NLU jobs.

I uploaded micro-benchmarks and the exact prompt sets we used here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cAcmeBenchmarks

If it helps, I can run a 24h regression sweep against your representative prompt set and provide quality delta numbers (BLEU / ROUGE / human pass rate) — that'll take ~2 business days.

—Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
